text:
jon: Quick follow-up to the routing RFC — do we all agree we should move from hard region-isolation rules to a region-weighted score that can be tuned per-tenant?

maria: leaning towards weighted scoring + hard exemptions for compliance tenants. gives flexibility for cost/latency tradeoffs.

kevin: agree. main concerns: 1) how we express this in the policy DSL, 2) interaction with reserved capacity (Dedicated) and SLA guarantees.

jon: sketch: score = alpha*latency_score + beta*cost_score + gamma*region_penalty + delta*tier_bonus. Policy DSL adds region_preference: { allow_cross_region: true/false, penalty: float }.

kevin: the DSL change looks ok. question: should the resolver return a single chosen route or an ordered candidate list with confidence? runtime needs fallback behavior if chosen node fails.

maria: ordered candidates + reasons. runtime can try first, then fallback to second. include explicit compatibility tags (quantized/seq-len) so fallbacks are safe.

jon: +1. also need per-tenant override that pins gamma very high for compliance. that should be surfaced as "policy.overrides.region_strict = true" at tenant scope.

kevin: about metrics: we need p50/p95/p99 latency per route, cost-per-token deltas from baseline, and fallback rate. can we add labels to traces for policy_reason and selected_rank?

sophia: yes. add tags: policy_reason, selected_candidate, candidate_score, fallback_used. will wire in to Console traces and Routing dashboards.

maria: migration plan proposal: 1) add scoring API in policy engine (no-op to runtime), 2) run scoring in parallel for a subset of traffic (shadow), 3) compare decisions vs current router, 4) start canary traffic where runtime uses score-derived order but still enforces per-tenant hard-exemptions, 5) expand.

jon: deployment note: Dedicated pools should be first-class in the scoring function. we need a term for reserved_capacity_penalty that prevents overloading dedicated-only models when shared is cheaper.

kevin: implementation note: cache resolved candidate lists keyed by (tenant, route_signature) with TTL tuned per model churn. invalidate on model rollout or capacity changes. avoid caching absolute scores — cache the ranked candidates and a version hash of policy+model-catalog.

maria: good call. also: ensure policy engine exposes an explain API: /resolve?tenant=...&signature=... -> {candidates: [...], reasons: [...], policy_hash}. useful for SRE debugging.

jon: security/compliance: for tenants with region_strict, the resolver must assert "region==allowed" before returning any cross-region candidate; tests should fail otherwise.

deploy-bot: deploy job queued: policy-engine/v2.3 -> staging at 2024-11-07T09:30Z :construction:

kevin: testing plan: create synthetic workload that biases latency/cost, assert that weighted routing moves traffic to cheaper region within SLO except when tenant pinned. inject network delay to check graceful fallback.

maria: final open question: do we keep a global default alpha/beta/gamma/delta, or compute them per-tenant from a heuristic?

jon: I'd prefer global defaults with tenant-scoped overrides. heuristics add complexity and surprising behavior for customers.

sophia: I'll add the telemetry dashboard mock and a small RFC addendum describing the DSL fields and sample tenant overrides.

jon: thanks — will draft the migration PR and link tests. if no objections by EOD we'll start the shadow run next week. :thumbsup:
